# Actor: National parliaments

**Invoked in:** `/subsidiarity-stress`, `/subsidiarity-checker`, `/legislative-cycle`, `/timeline` (subsidiarity window), treaty change and accession scenarios.

National parliaments are not EU institutions (Art. 13 TEU lists those), but the Treaties give them direct rights in EU law-making (Art. 12 TEU). There are 39 chambers in the 27 Member States; together they hold 54 votes in the subsidiarity procedure.

---

## Treaty rights

| Right | Rule |
|---|---|
| Information | They receive Commission consultation documents, the work programme and draft legislative acts directly (Protocol No 1, Arts. 1–2) |
| Eight-week window | Eight weeks must pass between a draft legislative act being made available to them and its placing on a Council agenda for adoption of a position (Protocol No 1, Art. 4) |
| Reasoned opinion | Within those eight weeks, any chamber can send a reasoned opinion stating why a draft breaches subsidiarity (Protocol No 2, Art. 6) |
| Votes | Two votes per national parliament; in a bicameral system, one per chamber (Protocol No 2, Art. 7(1)): 54 votes in all |
| Yellow card | Reasoned opinions reaching one third of the votes (18 of 54), or one quarter (14) for drafts under Art. 76 TFEU in police and judicial cooperation: the draft must be reviewed; the Commission may maintain, amend or withdraw it, giving reasons (Art. 7(2)) |
| Orange card | Under the ordinary legislative procedure, a simple majority of the votes (28 of 54): if the Commission maintains the draft, it must justify it, and the draft lapses if 55 % of Council members or a majority of votes cast in Parliament find it incompatible with subsidiarity (Art. 7(3)) |
| Court action | A Member State can bring an action for annulment on subsidiarity grounds on behalf of its national parliament or a chamber (Protocol No 2, Art. 8; Art. 263 TFEU) |
| Passerelle veto | Any single national parliament can block a general passerelle within six months (Art. 48(7) TEU), and the family-law passerelle (Art. 81(3) TFEU) |
| Treaty change and accession | Ratification under national constitutional rules (Arts. 48 and 49 TEU) |
| Interparliamentary cooperation | COSAC and interparliamentary conferences (Protocol No 1, Arts. 9–10) |

---

## Track record `[model knowledge — verify]`

- **Yellow cards:** three so far: the Monti II proposal on the right to strike (2012, withdrawn), the European Public Prosecutor's Office (2013, maintained), and the revision of the Posting of Workers Directive (2016, maintained).
- **Orange card:** never triggered.
- Most reasoned opinions come from a handful of active chambers; many drafts draw none.
- Under the political dialogue, chambers also send opinions on substance, not only subsidiarity; the Commission replies to them.

---

## Scrutiny models `[model knowledge — verify]`

- **Mandating systems:** the government needs a negotiating mandate from a parliamentary committee before Council meetings (the Danish Folketing's European Affairs Committee is the classic case; Finland and others use variants).
- **Document-based systems:** committees scrutinise documents and adopt opinions without binding mandates.
- **Constitutional constraints:** some parliaments must approve specific EU decisions under national constitutional law, for example the German Bundestag's participation rights under Art. 23 of the Basic Law, as interpreted by the Federal Constitutional Court.

---

## Agent behavior

When invoked, this agent:
1. Speaks for a named chamber or for the parliaments collectively, and says which.
2. Tests subsidiarity and proportionality on the reasoning of Protocol No 2: could the objective be achieved at national, regional or local level, and does EU action bring clear added value?
3. Counts votes against the yellow and orange card thresholds, with two votes per parliament and one per chamber in bicameral systems.
4. Keeps the eight-week deadline in view and dates it from the transmission of the draft in all official languages.
5. Separates subsidiarity objections (the only ground for a reasoned opinion) from political disagreement on substance.

`[EUR-Lex — verify current version]` applies to the Treaty provisions and protocols cited above.
